items.title: ترامپ، پوتین و شی پس از مذاکرات در چین، «بیانیه مشترک درباره صلح» منتشر کردند
items.summary: رهبران چین، آمریکا و روسیه پس از نشست سه‌جانبه بیانیه مشترکی منتشر کردند. در این بیانیه آمده است: «جنگ هسته‌ای برنده‌ای ندارد و هرگز نباید آغاز شود.» در این بیانیه همچنین آمده است که سه طرف درباره امنیت انرژی گفت‌وگو کرده‌اند و قصد دارند تولید و عرضه فرآورده‌های نفتی پالایش‌شده را افزایش دهند. در این بیانیه تاکیده شده است که رهبران چین، آمریکا و روسیه متعهد به حفظ «ثبات راهبردی و امنیت بین‌المللی» هستند.

items.summary: عربستان تایید کرد که بلندترین برج ریاض واقع در منطقه تجاری پایتخت، در حمله حوثی‌ها خسارت دیده است. سازمان دفاع مدنی عربستان می‌گوید چندین طبقه این ساختمان که «صندوق سرمایه ملی عربستان» را در خود جای داده آسیب دیده است. ساعاتی پیش سخنگوی ائتلاف عربستان گفته بود که ریزش بقایای یک موشک رهگیری شده در ریاض خسارت وارد کرده است. همان زمان شاهدان عینی از خسارت دیدن این برج خبر داده بودند.

items.summary_original: An imam who was scheduled to deliver the invocation at a city commission meeting Monday evening in a southwest Florida town was interrupted by Christian protesters — who had a prayer of their own to share. Footage from inside the meeting obtained by Fox News Digital shows dozens of Christian activists crowded into the back of a Bartow, Florida city commission meeting room. As Imam Sajid Bhuiya of the town's Masjid Al-Nur Mosque stepped up to the lectern to give the invocation, they began reciting the Lord's Prayer in unison. Some chants of "USA!" broke out, as well. According to Robert Goodman, the southeast regional director of the conservative activist group Citizens Defending Freedom, news of Bhuiya's scheduled appearance began making the rounds on social media last weekend. He was among those who shared the news on social media. Goodman said about 100 people from different groups ended up attending the meeting. items.summary_original: A former Southern Poverty Law Center official who led its hate-group tracking work told FBI agents he tried to make the watchdog’s controversial "Hate Map" more ideologically balanced, while saying Christians and conservatives were the first staffers pushed out in what he called a "long-term coup" at the organization after he left in 2013. The former director said he pushed for a more evenhanded SPLC, arguing that its "Hate Map" — which lists conservative groups alongside Ku Klux Klan chapters — should also include left-wing extremists, including violent animal-rights and extremist environmental groups. However, the former director said the effort met resistance and that, as liberal leaders reshaped the organization, most of his 17-person team was replaced. "There was some kind of coup, long-term coup going on there between some, what I would — what I heard were some pretty liberal people, extreme people that had other ideas about what we were doing," the unnamed former director told agents, as first reported by The Daily Signal's Tyler O'Neil , who has been covering the SPLC's legal troubles. items.summary_original: China's military could exploit advanced American technology, including through espionage and unauthorized access to artificial intelligence infrastructure, to develop weapons that could ultimately threaten U.S. forces, two congressional China watchdog leaders warned in an interview with Fox News Digital. The officials raised concerns that Beijing is seeking to acquire sophisticated U.S. semiconductors and access powerful AI data centers, potentially strengthening its military capabilities without the knowledge or involvement of the American companies behind the technology. Those concerns are underscored by the U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission's 2026 annual report , which says Beijing is seeking to circumvent American export controls to obtain advanced semiconductors for military modernization. The report describes Beijing's push toward "intelligentized warfare," integrating AI into weapons systems, targeting, military command and logistics. Mike Kuiken, the commission's vice chairman, warned that the threat extends beyond chip exports to access to computing infrastructure abroad. items.summary_original: Russian President Vladimir Putin vowed Thursday to respond to Ukraine in a "far more painful" manner after Volodymyr Zelenskyy's forces heavily damaged the Kerch Strait bridge that has become a symbol of Russia's annexation of Crimea. The warning was issued as Ukraine's president said he arrived in Berlin, Germany for talks with more than 40 partners aimed at ending the war, including with President Donald Trump's son-in-law and advisor Jared Kushner and U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff. "We will respond to these strikes. And I want everyone to know this: I believe our response will be far more painful than what the Kyiv regime did to the bridge," Putin said after meeting with President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping for trilateral talks on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, China, according to Reuters. "We will, of course, restore the bridge. The road section suffered serious damage," Putin reportedly added. UKRAINE RELEASE VIDEO SHOWING DAMAGE PUTIN'S PRIZE BRIDGE FOLLOWING 'UNPRECEDENTED OPERATION' IN CRIMEA Ukraine attacked the bridge for the third time this week prior to Putin making his remarks, Reuters reported. A Russian official told The Associated Press that the latest strike on the bridge linking Russia to Crimea halted rail traffic. items.summary_original: The European hometown of the man who single-handedly destroyed a U.S. military transport aircraft in an act of apparent protest has a rich history of pro-Palestinian support. This includes the town council for Cork, Ireland, barring Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu from entering its city limits, citing his "illegal occupation of Palestine and bordering countries" and the continuous pro-Palestinian protests taking place every Saturday since October 2023, organized by the Cork Palestine Solidarity Campaign (CPSC). Cork’s opposition to Israel adds context to the possible motives for why Daithí O’Corráin, an Irish national, allegedly destroyed a U.S. military C-130 Hercules aircraft in April. The incident also draws attention to several anti-Israel groups that have sprung up in Ireland in recent years. items.summary: الکساندریا اوکاسیو-کورتز، نماینده ایالت نیویورک، با افزایش گمانه زنی ها در مورد آینده سیاسی او، درها را برای نامزدی احتمالی ریاست جمهوری 2028 باز می گذارد. اوکاسیو کورتز در پاسخ به این سوال که آیا در حال بررسی نامزدی ریاست جمهوری در سال 2028 است، گفت: "من فکر می کنم، در حال حاضر، این انتخابات اتفاق افتاده است. ما باید برای به دست آوردن نتایج برای مردم کار کنیم." سازمان مترقی کمپین راه اندازی می کند و از AOC می خواهد برای ریاست جمهوری نامزد شود، در حالی که پیشروها به کاندیدای سوسیالیست چشم، اوکاسیو کورتز، که از سوسیالیست های دموکرات آمریکا (DSA) شعبه نیویورک سیتی برای یک پوت حمایت شده است.
items.summary_original: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., is leaving the door open to a potential 2028 presidential bid as speculation grows over her political future. "I think, right now, this election just happened. We got to work on getting results for people," Ocasio-Cortez told Fox News Digital when asked whether she was considering a presidential run in 2028. The self-described democratic socialist also expressed a willingness to work with President Donald Trump on key legislative priorities as Democrats prepare to take control of the House following the 2026 midterm elections. PROGRESSIVE ORG LAUNCHES CAMPAIGN URGING AOC TO RUN FOR PRESIDENT WHILE PROGRESSIVES EYE SOCIALIST CANDIDATE Ocasio-Cortez, who has drawn support from the Democratic Socialists of America's (DSA) New York City chapter for a potential White House bid, emphasized her desire to advance legislation in the 120th Congress rather than focus on presidential politics. Asked whether Democrats should work with Trump instead of prioritizing impeachment proceedings and congressional investigations , Ocasio-Cortez expressed optimism about finding common ground. "I hope so," she told Fox News Digital. "You know, I hope that President Trump can sign a congressional stock trading ban into law," Ocasio-Cortez continued. The congresswoman also identified healthcare reform as a potential area for bipartisan cooperation, urging Trump to address changes to Medicaid that she warned could threaten coverage for millions of Americans. items.summary_original: WASHINGTON, D.C. — Ice cream magnate Ben Cohen and activists from the far-left nonprofit CodePink packed into a lawmaker's office in House Longworth Building Room 1236 last week, demanding an end to the war in Iran, a cutoff of U.S. military ties to Israel and the removal of Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth. Next door, in House Rayburn Building Room 2267, Capitol police officers arrested far-left, anti-Israel demonstrators, including prolific street theater activist Hazami Barmada, cloaked in symbolic blood red, as they packed another lawmaker's office, condemning complicity in Israel's alleged "genocide" of Palestinians in Gaza. Across Capitol Hill in Senate Hart Building Room 322, police officers arrested young adults from a far-left nonprofit and political action committee, Sunrise Movement, as they packed a senator's office, condemning his politics, including his support of Israel. The next day, an activist from a far-left nonprofit, Climate Defiance, screamed at a high-ranking lawmaker speaking at a political conference, calling him a "traitor." But they weren't going after Republican lawmakers. They were far-left activists with a special target: The Democratic Party's leadership. items.summary_original: Rep. Nick Begich, R-Alaska, won re-election to Alaska’s lone House seat Wednesday, surviving a Democratic wave that flipped both the Senate seat and the governor’s mansion. Begich, who was endorsed by President Donald Trump, defeated independent challenger Bill Hill, a commercial fisherman and retired teacher backed by the Alaska Democratic Party, following the state’s ranked-choice voting tabulation. Begich’s victory, called at 9:27 p.m. ET on Wednesday – more than two weeks after Election Day – stood in sharp contrast to the rest of Alaska’s top-of-the-ticket results, where voters handed Democrats major breakthroughs despite Trump winning the state by 13% in 2024. HUNDREDS OF SUBPOENAS FLY IN DOJ’S ‘DECOY DAN’ PROBE AS DEMOCRAT PELTOLA DECLARED WINNER IN ALASKA The race was among the final House contests called nationally after the Nov. 3 general election, offering a rare bright spot for Republicans in a midterm cycle that saw Democrats seize control of both chambers of Congress. Democrats thus far hold a 257-172 majority in the House, having flipped 46 seats to just three for Republicans. There are three races that remain too close to call. "This process requires engagement, and the perspectives brought forward during the campaign added value for Alaskans as they made important decisions about their vote in this race," Begich said in a statement after his victory. items.summary_original: Chinese officials barred a Bloomberg reporter from a high-stakes meeting between President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin after she asked a question during an earlier bilateral session. The clash over press access unfolded on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Summit in Shenzhen, China , where the three leaders gathered for their first-ever three-way meeting to discuss nuclear arms control, trade and the wars in Ukraine and Iran. Despite a push from the White House to get her admitted, Chinese officials refused to budge on barring Bloomberg reporter Annmarie Hordern from the room. Hordern was blocked after she called out a question to Trump during his earlier one-on-one meeting with Xi: "President Trump, has Jensen Huang been disloyal to the United States?" CHINA'S XI SURPRISES TRUMP AT TARMAC, RECIPROCATING GESTURE SHOWN MONTHS AGO A second reporter also started to ask a question during the bilateral session but was shushed by Chinese officials. Beijing subsequently passed along a message to the U.S. travel pool warning that yelling questions is considered "extremely rude" and that journalists would be pulled from the room if they did so. A White House official, speaking on condition of anonymity because of the sensitivity surrounding the issue, said Chinese officials insisted Hordern not be allowed into the trilateral meeting even as the White House advocated for her inclusion. "Sometimes this manifests as verbal or physical violence, attacks, arson, property damage and, among other things, agricultural terrorism involving harm to animals." items.summary_original: There's nonzero chance Democrats could kick off their newfound dominance on Capitol Hill with another government shutdown . Several House Republicans told Fox News Digital they were worried about Democrats in both chambers making unreasonable and highly partisan demands ahead of the Dec. 11, 2026, federal funding deadline, potentially paralyzing the U.S. government until a deal could be reached. "I’m concerned," Rep. Ryan Zinke, R-Mont., told Fox News Digital. "I would say it is on my threat button, as a SEAL, it’s a five-meter target." Rep. Mike Haridopolos, R-Fla., suggested Democrats' recent midterm victories would give them the confidence to allow a shutdown to happen. REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK: CONGRESS DODGED A FALL SHUTDOWN, BUT THE REAL FIGHT LOOMS "I’m very worried about it. Unfortunately, the Democrat tactics of shutting down the government worked for them politically, so I’m afraid they’re going to go back to their winning playbook," he said. items.summary_original: President Donald Trump joined the leaders of China and Russia Thursday for an unprecedented three-way summit, marking a historic moment in global diplomacy as the three powers discussed nuclear arms reductions, the war in Ukraine and global security without announcing a major breakthrough. The unprecedented three-way meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin underscored the leaders' commitment to continued diplomacy, with Trump emphasizing the importance of maintaining dialogue among rival nuclear powers. Trump left the trilateral meeting, which lasted more than an hour, around 5 a.m. ET and headed to the airport. He is not expected to deliver public remarks before flying back to Washington, Fox News reported. "We are really making history," Trump declared during the meeting in Shenzhen, China, as he sought to cast the gathering itself as a diplomatic achievement. CHINA WATCHDOG WARNS TRUMP FACES ‘2-ON-1’ SHOWDOWN WITH XI, PUTIN AS TAIWAN RISKS MOUNT The three leaders sat down at a roundtable just after 3 a.m. ET, roughly two hours behind schedule. Trump argued that bringing the three leaders together offered an opportunity to address issues that had long divided their countries. "Too often, past leaders avoided talking to nations with whom they had disagreements," Trump said. "But no problems were ever solved under the old school refusing to talk about them." items.summary_original: A Trump administration official who served four months in federal prison for defying a congressional subpoena is asking the Supreme Court to overturn his convictions in a case that could raise the bar for criminally prosecuting others who refuse to comply with Congress’s demands. Peter Navarro, who was a senior trade advisor to President Donald Trump during his first administration, filed a petition with the Supreme Court last month. Navarro currently serves in the Trump administration as senior counselor for trade and manufacturing. He was convicted in 2023 on two counts of contempt of Congress stemming from his refusal to provide testimony and documents to the Democratic-led House Jan. 6 committee on the grounds that he believed he was barred by executive privilege. If the justices take the case, they could make it harder to convict someone for defying a congressional subpoena by requiring proof that the person knew they were breaking the law. JUDGE TOSSES CASE AGAINST EX-FBI OFFICIALS ACCUSED OF LYING TO CONGRESS ABOUT HUNTER BIDEN INVESTIGATION Before Navarro’s trial, U. S. District Judge Amit Mehta ruled in August 2023 that he had failed to establish that Trump invoked executive privilege for the subpoena, barring him from relying on that claim as a defense. After serving his sentence, Navarro appealed his conviction to the U. S. Court of Appeals for the D. C. items.summary_original: A Somali politician whose daycare business has been tied to fraud is married to an illegal alien, Fox News Digital has confirmed. Minnesota Democratic–Farmer–Labor Party (DFL) candidate Abdi Daisane defeated a Republican incumbent to win Minnesota’s House District 14A seat, which encompasses some of the city of St. Cloud. Daisane's wife, Ayaan Aydid, 30, is present in the country illegally, a Trump administration official confirmed on Wednesday afternoon after an Alpha News report on the subject. Aydid crossed the U.S. southern border with Mexico in 2023, during former President Joe Biden's administration. An accompanying story describes Aydid as "one of hundreds of Somalis who have jumped the US-Mexico border wall." "It wasn't a hard journey," she said in the interview. Daisane, who delivered part of his victory speech in Somali, is the CEO of Blooming Kids Child Care Center in St. Cloud, which has received $7.29 million from the state-run Child Care Assistance Program since 2018. The gathering in Shenzhen culminated in the first-ever trilateral meeting between the leaders of the United States, China and Russia, with nuclear arms reductions and the war in Ukraine among the issues on the table. Here are some of the standout moments from Trump's visit. XI BREAKS PROTOCOL TO PERSONALLY WELCOME TRUMP AHEAD OF HISTORIC TRILATERAL SUMMIT AND MORE TOP HEADLINES Trump declared the United States the world leader in "superintelligence" during remarks at the summit Thursday, making the assertion in one of China's major technology hubs. "The United States is also proud to be the world leader in superintelligence, the greatest technological transformation since the Industrial Revolution," Trump told APEC leaders. The remarks came as Washington and Beijing compete for leadership in artificial intelligence and advanced semiconductors . Trump joined Xi and Putin for the first-ever trilateral meeting between the leaders of the United States, China and Russia just after 3 a.m. ET, calling the gathering an opportunity to reduce nuclear weapons and address global conflicts. items.summary_original: President Donald Trump 's proposed 250-foot triumphal arch near Arlington in Washington, D.C., was dealt another blow Wednesday when a federal judge extended an order blocking construction until at least early December. U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan extended her initial Nov. 5 temporary restraining order blocking construction of the arch for another 14 days, delaying progress on the structure until at least Dec. 3. The extension comes as Chutkan's original order was set to expire Thursday. The judge said the extension would give her additional time to consider lawsuits filed by the District of Columbia and Virginia seeking a longer-term injunction against the project. MULTIPLE KENNEDY FAMILY MEMBERS SEEK TO JOIN LEGAL BATTLE AGAINST TRUMP'S TRIUMPHAL ARCH The order marks the latest setback for one of the president's major projects in the nation's capital. Inspired by Paris' Arc de Triomphe, the proposed monument would stand near the Memorial Bridge, which connects Arlington National Cemetery to Washington, D.C. In a statement to Fox News Digital, the White House criticized the order, saying the project was being undercut by an "activist district court." "The judiciary should not be abused to politicize a structure designed to unite our nation," White House spokesman Davis Ingle said. "We will continue making the case for this beautiful and fitting monument and are confident we will be fully vindicated as this litigation proceeds," he added. EXCAVATION SET TO BEGIN ON TRUM

items.summary: جلسه شورای شهر ساکرامنتو روز سه‌شنبه پس از اینکه یکی از ساکنان خشمگین زندگی سیاسی شهردار دموکرات را تهدید کرد و سعی کرد آدرس خانه‌اش را به طور علنی فاش کند، به هرج و مرج منجر شد و مقامات را بر آن داشت تا میکروفون او را قطع کنند و جلسه را موقتاً متوقف کنند. ویدئویی از پخش زنده شورای شهر روز سه‌شنبه که توسط فاکس نیوز دیجیتال بازبینی شده بود، زنی را نشان می‌دهد که با کوین مک کارتی، شهردار ساکرامنتو، در طول بخش نظرات عمومی جلسه روبرو می‌شود و هشدار می‌دهد که اگر مقامات نتوانند به نگرانی‌هایشان رسیدگی کنند، معترضان به اختلال در تجارت شهر ادامه خواهند داد. زن گفت: "اگر دوباره به نفع ما رای ندهی، پشیمان می شوی." "ما اعتراض می کنیم. کارها را متوقف می کنیم. کارها را تعطیل می کنیم، کوین. و مشاغل." سپس زن پیشنهاد کرد که حرفه سیاسی مک کارتی مسیر خود را طی کرده است. شهر ممفیس
items.summary_original: A Sacramento City Council meeting descended into chaos Tuesday after an angry resident threatened the Democratic mayor's political career and attempted to publicly reveal his home address, prompting officials to cut her microphone and temporarily recess the meeting. Video from Tuesday's City Council livestream reviewed by Fox News Digital showed a woman confronting Sacramento Mayor Kevin McCarty during the public comment portion of the meeting, warning that protesters would continue disrupting city business if officials failed to address their concerns. "If you do not vote in our interest again, you will regret it," the woman said. "We protest. We stop things. We shut things down, Kevin. And careers." The woman then suggested that McCarty's political career had run its course. MEMPHIS CITY COUNCIL DEVOLVES INTO CHAOS AFTER DATA CENTER MORATORIUM VOTE POSTPONED "It's time for your f---ing career to end," she said, before raising the possibility of his retirement. As council officials repeatedly attempted to restore order, someone in the audience also urged the angry woman to show decorum. "F--- your decorum," she responded. The confrontation escalated further when the woman threatened to disclose the mayor's home address. "I do not give a f--- about your privacy," she shouted. "Do you want everyone to know your address? items.summary_original: Thousands of people in Haiti took to the streets Tuesday in a show of support for Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele deploying troops to the country to combat violent armed gangs. The demonstration unfolded as Haiti's Minister of Justice and Public Security, Patrick Pélissier, prepared to travel to San Salvador to discuss anti-gang strategies and ongoing troop cooperation. The president reflected on the moment in a post on X, sharing a video capturing a sea of people chanting, dancing and cheering in celebration. "I never expected anything like this. I hear you loud and clear. I love you too. We will triumph. God will give us victory," Bukele said. BUKELE WARNS HAITIAN GANG LEADERS THAT HIS FORCES WILL 'FINISH' THEM AS HE DID IN EL SALVADOR According to Reuters, some demonstrators carried signs reading "Long live Bukele" and "Down with the gangs," while others voiced their support for the Salvadoran leader. "Only a week of operation, we can see the path to change in Haiti. We say thank you to Bukele for all the help he gives us," demonstrator Claudy Mayas said. Another demonstrator said Bukele was providing Haitians with the one thing they had been waiting years for. "Four years ago, I could not go to Champs de Mars. I couldn't go to the south of Haiti," a demonstrator, also identified as Claude, said. "We don’t ask much of the government. We don’t ask for jobs. We need only security." items.summary_original: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) warned Wednesday that Bahrain's monarchy faces an existential threat as Iranian drones and missiles targeted U.S. military installations in the Gulf kingdom. Tehran's warning came amid renewed attacks on Bahrain, home to the U.S. Navy's Fifth Fleet, and a regional expert warned of Iran's decades-long efforts to destabilize the island nation and assert territorial claims. "This is a regime that has tried to inflame tensions there for quite literally several decades and has claims to the island nation as well," Behnam Ben Taleblu , a senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD), told Fox News Digital. BAHRAIN INTERCEPTS IRANIAN DRONES TARGETING US RADAR AFTER 2-MONTH LULL IN GULF STRIKES "The Islamic Republic is also trying to use military force to evict the United States from the region," he added. In a warning directed at Bahrain's ruling Al Khalifa family, IRGC Brig. Gen. Hossein Mohebbi accused the monarchy of cooperating with military action against Iran , relying on U.S. protection and challenging Shiite religious authority. "Colluding in the aggression against Islamic Iran, living inside the American security bubble, and encroaching on the authority of the Shiite religious leadership are three fundamental mistakes being made by the Al Khalifa regime," Mohebbi wrote on X . items.summary_original: People practicing the Islamic faith are poised to outnumber Christians globally by 2035, becoming the world's largest religion, according to a new study released by the Pew Research Center. The detailed report attributes the shift primarily to higher fertility rates and younger populations among Muslims, who are growing at a faster rate than other major faiths. "Around the world, we find that Muslims tend to have more children than non-Muslims, [and] they tend to be younger as a result of having more children in the past," Pew senior demographer Conrad Hackett told Fox News Digital. WHY PEOPLE REALLY STOPPED HAVING KIDS: NEW STUDY UNCOVERS THE SURPRISING REASONS FAMILIES ARE SHRINKING Muslims have the highest fertility rate at 3.1 children per woman, followed by Christians at 2.5, according to the study. Between 2020 and 2025, Muslim women gave birth to 252 million babies, more than women of any other religion and compared to 208 million born to Christian mothers. If trends continue, the United States will also undergo a major religious shift . While Christians currently account for roughly 62% to 64% of U. Federal prosecutors announced the indictment Tuesday, seven months after Daithi O'Corrain, 48, allegedly breached the security perimeter at Shannon Airport in western Ireland and broke into an unoccupied U.S. Air National Guard C-130H Hercules aircraft. Photographs released by federal prosecutors show extensive damage inside the aircraft, including smashed cockpit instruments, severed wiring and damaged equipment. Other images show tools allegedly used in the attack and O'Corrain standing on the aircraft's roof before his arrest. items.summary_original: The U.S. Army turned to one of the year’s most anticipated video games to get soldiers at Fort Stewart, Georgia, talking about reenlisting. The offer was a four-day pass to play " Grand Theft Auto VI " when it launches Thursday. The Army said 43 of the 130 eligible soldiers in the 9th Brigade Engineer Battalion chose the perk when they reenlisted for two to six more years, Task Purpose first reported. NBA PLAYER PREDICTS AMERICAN ATHLETES' PERFORMANCES WILL DIP IN NOVEMBER WHILE THEY PLAY GTA "I’m all campaign. I’m all about the heist," Sgt. Jamire Smith, a combat engineer who signed up for six more years in the Army and took the four-day pass, told Task Purpose. "I think I have a good 24 hours to waste on it." Smith said he had been close to leaving the Army before leaders in his company and battalion showed him they still needed his skills. He qualified for a roughly $60,000 reenlistment bonus after training to drive heavy breaching vehicles, the outlet reported. US ARMY HITS 2026 RECRUITING GOALS FOUR MONTHS EARLY, PETE HEGSETH ANNOUNCES AT WEST POINT COMMENCEMENT The battalion offered the pass from Aug. 1 through Nov. 14. The Army said the time off came on top of standard reenlistment incentives , which can include cash bonuses or a choice of duty station depending on a soldier’s eligibility and the Army’s needs. items.summary_original: The U.S. Army is racing to hire contractors to build 17 reinforced concrete bunkers in Israel, Saudi Arabia and Lebanon to protect American and coalition troops from deadly missile and drone attacks, according to a government procurement notice posted Friday. The move comes amid escalating violence in the Middle East , where Iranian attacks on U.S. military installations have killed at least 23 American service members since war broke out in late February. On Tuesday, Iran also claimed responsibility for another strike on a U.S. military base in Bahrain, its third attack there in five days. BAHRAIN INTERCEPTS IRANIAN DRONES TARGETING US RADAR AFTER 2-MONTH LULL IN GULF STRIKES Kuwaiti air defenses also intercepted incoming drones as Israeli forces launched new strikes in eastern and southern Lebanon. The Army plans to build 10 bunkers in Israel, five in Saudi Arabia and two in Lebanon, replacing makeshift shelters made from shipping containers. "Due to elevated regional force protection conditions, there is an urgent, high-priority requirement to replace nonstandard personnel protection shelters (e.g., converted shipping containers) and provide standardized, precast, reinforced concrete Indirect Fire bunkers," the Army said in the notice. "The objective is to safeguard U.S. and coalition service members operating in potentially hostile environments across multiple countries in [U.S. Central Command] Area of Responsibility," the notice added. items.summary_original: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un is accelerating his nuclear program, expanding a uranium enrichment facility that can produce plutonium for nuclear weapons, the United Nations' nuclear watchdog warned Wednesday, calling Pyongyang's growing program a "cause for serious concern." International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) Director General Rafael Grossi said the latest construction at the Yongbyon nuclear complex began in mid-September and was externally complete by late October, raising fresh alarms about North Korea's production of weapons-grade nuclear material. "The ongoing expansion of the DPRK's uranium enrichment programme remains a cause for serious concern," Grossi said in remarks to the IAEA's board of governors in Vienna , referring to North Korea by its official name, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea. items.summary_original: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin defended letting travelers keep their shoes on at airport checkpoints Wednesday after an Arizona congressman pressed him on why the TSA policy remains in place despite a classified watchdog review. "We have never put anyone at risk at all," Mullin told Rep. Eli Crane, R-Ariz., at a House Homeland Security Committee hearing . Mullin said the department evaluates screening technology daily and that he had personally met with DHS Inspector General Joseph Cuffari in a secure facility. "In fact, we addressed three of the four concerns," Mullin said. He said the fourth, in his view, had nothing to do with security. TLAIB MOVES TO BLOCK ICE AIRPORT ARRESTS, SAYS TSA HELPING TARGET IMMIGRANTS Mullin gave no specifics about what DHS had done to address the three concerns or what the fourth involved. Crane said he had received a classified briefing from the inspector general and called it "very concerning." He asked Mullin to discuss the matter privately. The exchange put renewed scrutiny on a July 2025 decision by then-Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem to end routine shoe removal at TSA checkpoints nationwide. Noem said at the time that advances in screening technology would allow the agency to speed up lines while maintaining security. TSA officers could still ask travelers to remove their shoes for additional screening. The high-stakes talks are expected to address issues such as the wars in Ukraine and Iran, trade and nuclear weapons. Mike Kuiken, the commission's vice chairman, echoed Schriver's assessment, arguing that Moscow's growing dependence on Beijing puts Trump at a disadvantage. items.summary_original: EXCLUSIVE: The Justice Department has issued more than 200 subpoenas in its criminal investigation into Dan J. Sullivan — "Decoy Dan" — who ran against Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan in Alaska's U.S. Senate race, Fox News Digital has learned. News of the scope of the sprawling criminal probe comes after Democrat Mary Peltola was officially declared the winner of the four-way general election on Tuesday night — two weeks after Election Day. She won 144,302 votes to the incumbent Sullivan's 131,844. A GOP candidate named Gerald Heikes won 6,105 votes, while so-called "Decoy Dan" won 4,760 votes as a non-party affiliated candidate. A law enforcement source says the criminal case is continuing, and that Peltola being named the winner doesn't change anything from an investigative standpoint. The DOJ's investigation spans multiple states, and there are multiple criminal targets in the case, the source said. A second source familiar with the investigation confirmed that more than 200 subpoenas have been issued. Allegations have swirled that Democrats searched for a person with the name Dan Sullivan to run against the incumbent senator of the same name in order to confuse voters and potentially spoil the Republicans' chances of reelection. items.summary_original: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., brushed off opposition from far-left Democrats during Wednesday's caucus vote, which overwhelmingly nominated him to become the next House speaker. Speaking after the vote, Jeffries said he expects the incoming Democratic majority to "work together." Only 11 Democrats voted against Jeffries' nomination. Among those who opposed him — or intended to — were Reps.-elect Darializa Avila Chevalier, Adam Hamawy, Frederick D. Haynes III, Melat Kiros, Donavan McKinney, Chris Rabb and Claire Valdez. FOLLOW THE LEADER: DEMOCRATS FACE PARTY BATTLE AS DIVISIONS DEEPEN In a joint statement, the group noted that discussions with Jeffries regarding their legislative priorities remain "ongoing." "Whether on Medicare-for-all , stopping ICE terror, getting money out of politics or ending the genocide in Gaza, our constituents sent us to Congress with a mandate on these issues," the incoming lawmakers said in their statement. "We have worked to secure commitments from Leader Jeffries in good-faith conversations." ‘SQUAD’ MEMBER ANNOUNCES ‘MAJORITY PRIORITIES’ INCLUDING REPARATIONS, ABOLISHING ICE AFTER BLUE WAVE When asked about the dissenting votes, Jeffries said the caucus' election results spoke for themselves. He declined to say whether he would adopt the far left's policy demands, which include abolishing U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and ending military aid to Israel . Most notably, Houston Mayor John Whitmire issued a Nov. 6 executive order telling the city's police officers that they are no longer permitted to notify ICE if they encounter an illegal immigrant during a nonviolent encounter. DEMOCRAT GINA HINOJOSA STUNS ABBOTT, MAKES HISTORY AS FIRST LATINA TEXAS GOVERNOR Shortly after Whitmire's order, the mayors of Austin and San Antonio also issued executive orders limiting city police cooperation with ICE. "If Texas were to stop cooperating with ICE and become a sanctuary state , it would be one of the worst derelictions of duty we’ve seen in a very long time," Mullin told Fox exclusively. "The Ilsky Oil Refinery is one of the largest oil refineries in southern Russia, with an annual processing capacity of approximately 6.6 million tons of crude oil. items.summary_original: Protesters heckled former Trump Border Patrol commander-at-large Gregory Bovino off stage during a Monday night speech at Rutgers University, hours after New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill called the Rutgers College Republicans’ decision to host him "wrong" and urged the club to reconsider. Bovino previously criticized Sherrill online, accusing her of prioritizing illegal immigrants over New Jersey residents. After returning to the stage, he called her "Sugar Pop Sherrill" and "Kim Jong Sherrill." Speaking to reporters afterward, he said she wanted to "trounce this freedom of speech ," described the "Kim Jong Sherrill" label as "very fitting" and called the governor a "totalitarian." He also told Blaze News that Sherrill had timed her social media comments to "foment violence" against conservatives. At Monday night’s Rutgers College Republicans event, protesters began shouting within minutes of Bovino taking the stage. Rutgers police escorted him offstage and ordered the hecklers to leave or face arrest, according to local reports. Bovino returned about ten minutes later to resume his remarks and answer questions. items.summary_original: More than a dozen Ecuadorian fishermen have sued the federal government, alleging they were wrongly targeted in a drone strike that destroyed their boat in the Pacific Ocean earlier this year as part of the Trump administration’s broader campaign against vessels suspected of drug trafficking. The 16 fishermen aboard La Negra Francisca Duarte II say drones launched from a U.S. vessel struck their boat March 17, 2026, as they headed home from a two-week fishing trip near the Galápagos. The strike set the boat ablaze, forcing the crew to jump overboard and escape in lifeboats, according to a lawsuit filed Monday in federal court in Pennsylvania. All 16 survived, but two suffered serious burns. One man’s leg was burned to the bone, the lawsuit says. The fishermen’s lawyers say the crew had no ties to drug cartels or terrorist groups and posed no imminent threat when U.S. drones struck their vessel, which they say had been cleared by Ecuadorian authorities hours earlier. US MILITARY LAUNCHES FIRST AUTONOMOUS WARFARE COMMAND TO DEPLOY UNMANNED SYSTEMS ACROSS LATIN AMERICA After their boat was destroyed, the fishermen sailed toward a blue vessel, which the lawsuit identified as a U.S. ship. Some personnel wore U.S. Coast Guard vests, the suit says. They allegedly zip-tied the uninjured men, hooded them and forced them to stand barefoot on the hot metal deck with no food and little water. items.summary_original: CodePink co-founder Medea Benjamin’s $54.6 million family foundation has been reinstated as a California charity after years of missed financial filings, although questions linger over $2.7 million in grants it reported paying in 2024, the year its registration was suspended. The foundation, Arc of Justice, has poured $24.6 million into protest groups, legal advocacy organizations and progressive nonprofits over more than two decades, a previous Fox News Digital investigation found . The 2024 payouts included $350,000 to CodePink, according to the foundation’s 2024 federal tax return. Years of missed filings prompted regulators in California to revoke the foundation's charitable registration in January 2025 after more than a year of suspension for repeatedly failing to submit required annual reports or respond to regulatory notices. State regulators restored it in September, placing the foundation on three years probation. $54M CODEPINK-LINKED FOUNDATION SHUT DOWN IN CALIFORNIA POPS UP AT RAMSHACKLE MIAMI HOME Under California regulations, organizations with suspended or revoked charitable registrations are prohibited from distributing or spending charitable assets without the attorney general’s prior written approval, according to Title 11, Section 345(b) of to the California Code of Regulations . items.summary_original: Recent service outages across U.S. systems stem from routine technical and maintenance issues – not a coordinated foreign cyberattack, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton testified Wednesday, even as he warned lawmakers that "superintelligence" is rapidly escalating the speed and sophistication of future cyber threats. "Based on what we know today, after a great deal of digital diligence, these are separate service outages associated with maintenance and technical changes, " Clayton told the House Homeland Security Committee's "Worldwide Threats to the Homeland: 25 Years After 9/11" hearing. "They are not a coordinated or state-sponsored attack." Clayton acknowledged public concern over the timing of the recent outages, telling the panel that the American people are right to ask questions, but intelligence reviews point away from foreign interference. THE OUTAGES AMERICA HAS SUFFERED WEREN'T AN ATTACK, BUT THE NEXT FAILURE COULD BE "We have no indication that these events are related," Clayton said in response to persistent questioning from Rep. Dan Goldman, D-N.Y. "But let me answer something that the American people should know, which is the speed of compute and the level of capability of applications that use that compute is increasing substantially, which means legacy systems that were old six months ago or a year are a lot older." items.summary: صدها ایرانی با شعار مرگ بر دیکتاتور به خیابان ها ریختند. گزارش‌ها حاکی از آن است که در پی تصادف مرگبار اتوبوس در آخر هفته که منجر به کشته شدن 13 کارمند یک شرکت پالایشگاه نفت شد، و سایر پیام‌های ضد دولتی. نمایش نادر خشم ضد دولتی روز سه شنبه در آبدانان، شهری در غرب ایران در نزدیکی مرز این کشور با عراق آشکار شد. تظاهرکنندگان خواستار استعفای مقامات شرکتی شدند که عامل این حادثه هستند. به گزارش خبرگزاری میزان به نقل از رادیو اروپای آزاد، امرالله میسایی، دادستان محلی گفت: با کسانی که از این حادثه برای اخلال در نظم عمومی و تحریک عواطف مردم سوء استفاده کنند، قاطعانه برخورد خواهد شد. این رسانه به نقل از خبرگزاری فارس ایران همچنین گزارش داد که حدود 1000 نفر در این تظاهرات شرکت کردند.
items.summary_original: Hundreds of Iranians took to the streets chanting "Death to the dictator!" and other anti-government messages in the wake of a deadly bus crash over the weekend that killed 13 employees of an oil refinery company, reports said. The rare display of anti-government anger unfolded Tuesday in Abdanan, a city in western Iran near the country's border with Iraq. Demonstrators called for the resignation of company officials blamed for the accident. "Those who seek to exploit this incident to disrupt public order and inflame people’s emotions will be dealt with decisively," local prosecutor Amrollah Meysaei was quoted by Iran's Mizan news agency as saying, according to Radio Free Europe. The outlet, citing Iran's Fars news agency, also reported that an estimated 1,000 people took part in the protests, making them the largest demonstrations since mass unrest swept across Iran at the beginning of this year. Some of the protesters reportedly tried to damage public property. Mamdani and Ossé, D-Brooklyn, announced this week that the Strategic Response Group (SRG) will be dissolved in alignment with a key campaign promise by the mayor, as critics, including former NYPD Commissioner Bill Bratton, who created the unit, warn it will make the nation’s largest city more dangerous. "Florida is always looking for well-qualified new officers," Sen. Ashley Moody , R-Fla., said in reaction to the news. NYPD officers who accept the invitation would add to the nearly 376,000 New Yorkers who relocated to Florida between 2019 and 2023, according to figures reported by New York's WPIX-11 News . Miami-Dade County Commissioner Roberto Gonzalez, a Republican, also issued a call for disillusioned NYPD officers to relocate. items.summary_original: Eight decades after the Holocaust , Germany's conservative Chancellor Friedrich Merz warned that accepting the nation's responsibility for the Nazi genocide is an obligation that extends fully to immigrants arriving from Islamic countries. During an official reception for Germany’s Maccabiah Jewish sports delegation in Berlin on Nov. 6, Merz said the "historical responsibility of our country applies just as much to those who come here to Germany from Islamic countries, and anyone who fails to abide by this must leave our country." His response came after a basketball coach told him athletes feared being attacked if they wore their red Maccabi training jackets bearing the Star of David on German streets. The German Press Agency, dpa, reported that Merz quoted former German President Richard von Weizsäcker, who in 1985 told the Bundestag that "young people are not responsible" for the crimes of the Nazis, "but they are responsible for what becomes of it in history." Merz said the principle was "set in stone," and that, "given the current circumstances," von Weizsäcker’s words "also apply to immigrants who come to Germany," referring to recent antisemitic offenses committed by Muslim immigrants. items.summary_original: Pope Leo XIV broke his silence Monday after being struck in the face by a rosary thrown by a worshipper in Peru, joking about the incident while also revealing details for the very first time about his cancer diagnosis and major surgery which took place before his recent trip to South America. The pope, who had the lower lobe of his right lung removed Oct. 13, after doctors found a cancerous tumor , told reporters on the flight home to Rome that he has not fully recovered, but said he was determined to complete the long-planned 12-day journey. "Just over a month ago, as everybody knows, I underwent rather major surgery," Leo, 71, said during a roughly 45-minute news conference on board the papal plane returning from Lima, Peru. POPE LEO WELCOMED BACK AS HE DELIVERS ANGELUS PRAYER DAYS AFTER LUNG CANCER SURGERY "But from the very beginning, I had in mind that this trip had been planned and that I was going to make it happen." The pontiff credited his recovery to prayer, medical care and personal determination. "So, with God's help — and I firmly believe in the power of prayer, as I have literally received messages from all over the world — together with a certain personal determination, which I also have, and with the help of the doctors, it proved to be possible." Despite the demanding itinerary that included multiple flights and appearances before massive crowds in Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, Leo acknowledged that he is still regaining his strength. Other photographs show his daughter skiing in an all-white outfit as officials navigate the slopes nearby. The girl, believed to be named Kim Ju Ae, has increasingly appeared alongside her father at high-profile public events. South Korea's National Intelligence Service has assessed that she is being positioned as his likely successor, although North Korea has not publicly confirmed a succession plan. In an exclusive interview with The Press Service of Israel (TPS-IL) published Tuesday, Huckabee rejected the argument that Israel was responsible for the GOP’s electoral defeat, instead pointing to economic concerns, voter apathy and a failure to energize the Republican base. "Israel was not the reason the elections went wrong for Republicans last week," Huckabee told TPS-IL . TRUMP ADMITS IRAN WAR CONTRIBUTED TO GOP MIDTERM LOSSES, INSISTS IT WAS NECESSARY The remarks come nearly two weeks after Vance blamed Republican losses on the war with Iran and dissatisfaction with Washington’s relationship with Israel. "The reason we lost is the war," Vance wrote, arguing that the party needed to acknowledge the political consequences of the conflict. items.summary_original: An Israeli-Russian researcher held hostage for 903 days by an Iran-backed Iraqi terrorist group revealed to Fox News Digital that she spent the first four and a half months of her captivity inside the very militia stronghold Iraq's Trump-backed prime minister has now ordered the army to reclaim. Elizabeth Tsurkov, a senior nonresident fellow at the New Lines Institute for Strategy and Policy, said Kata’ib Hezbollah turned a private family's home in Jurf al-Sakhr, south of Baghdad, into a prison where she was held captive. "This is where I was held for 4.5 months," Tsurkov told Fox News Digital in an interview, referring to the early months of her captivity, which began with her abduction in Baghdad in March 2023. "I was held in a private home of a family that was taken over by Kata’ib Hezbollah and turned into a prison," she said. TRUMP ADMIN WARNS IRAQ OVER IRAN TERROR PROXIES AS US REPORTEDLY BLOCKS CASH PAYMENTS Tsurkov, who was freed in September 2025 following negotiations and sustained pressure from the Trump administration to secure her release, said that any effort to reclaim the territory must go far beyond dismantling alleged oil-smuggling operations. She called for Iraqi authorities to search the sprawling area, including surrounding towns and villages, for "secret prisons," "mass burial sites" and "storage facilities for weapons," and to return confiscated homes to their rightful owners. items.summary_original: The Security Service of Ukraine released two videos Tuesday showing the aftermath of a devastating drone attack on Russian President Vladimir Putin's prized Crimea bridge. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday's attack on the Kerch Strait bridge was part of an "unprecedented operation in response to Russian strikes on our infrastructure." "Today, everyone can see the consequences for the main military crossing from Russian territory into our Ukrainian Crimea," Zelenskky wrote on X. "This is the result of the seventh stage of an operation carried out over several weeks ... Our warriors gradually destroyed air defense systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment, and other designated targets on the way to the final objective. "Today, at the key stage, the 'Palianytsia' drones performed exceptionally well, striking the road section of the bridge, while 'Neptune' missiles, 'Ruta' drones, and FP-5 drones struck the railway section. Using 'Flamingo,' our warriors carried out a precision-guided strike – and the communications uplink worked flawlessly until the very last seconds," Zelenskyy added. items.title: چند روایت از ایران در رسانه‌های آمریکا؛ از ادعای ربودن دو فرمانده سپاه توسط موساد تا آینده فشارهای اقتصادی
items.summary: نیویورک تایمز در گزارشی تحقیقی مدعی شده است که موساد در جریان تلاش چند دهه‌ای برای روشن کردن سرنوشت رون آراد، خلبان مفقودشده اسرائیلی، دو فرمانده سپاه پاسداران را در دو عملیات جداگانه ربوده است. این روزنامه همچنین به نقل از مقام‌های پیشین آمریکایی گزارش داده که یکی از این افراد، علیرضا عسگری، پس از هفته‌ها بازجویی کشته شد. به نوشته نیویورک تایمز، این اقدامات در حالی انجام شده که برخی ارزیابی‌های اطلاعاتی اسرائیل به شواهد قانع‌کننده‌ای درباره نقش ایران در ناپدید شدن آراد دست نیافته بودند.
